title: Week 05 · Architecture Decision Lab — From Discovery to Technical Direction
description: A 50-minute architecture decision session that converts discovery evidence into a defensible technical direction. Students define system boundaries, map data and components, pressure-test assumptions and risks, receive expert challenge, make a milestone gate decision, and leave with explicit ownership.

steps.label: OPEN
steps.title: What do we know now that we did not know two weeks ago?
steps.lead: Architecture should begin with evidence, not imagination.
steps.studentTask: Each team names 2–3 discovery findings that materially change what should be designed or built.
steps.visualAccent: Do not design from memory. Design from evidence.
steps.visualCaption: What changed? What became clearer? What assumption was weakened or confirmed?

runbook.openWith: Today is the bridge from discovery to architecture. I do not want a tour of everything you did. I want the evidence that should change a technical decision.
runbook.whyMatters: Prevents architecture theater and forces teams to anchor technical choices in current evidence.
runbook.ask: What do we know now that we did not know two weeks ago?
runbook.listenFor: User needs, data realities, system constraints, accuracy requirements, workflow realities, access limitations, client expectations.
runbook.ifTheySay: We learned a lot → ask for the one finding that should change the system.
runbook.ifQuiet: Ask each team to name one assumption that is now stronger or weaker.
runbook.pushFurther: If this finding disappeared, would your architecture change?
runbook.sayDuringReveal: If the evidence does not change a decision, it may be useful context—but it is not yet architecture evidence.
runbook.landHere: Architecture starts with what the team can defend.
runbook.transition: Now draw the boundary around what this system is actually responsible for.
runbook.studentDoes: Identifies discovery findings with architectural consequences.
runbook.askNext: What does the system need to own—and what should remain outside it?
runbook.ifStuck: Use the stem: We observed ____, therefore the system should/should not ____.
runbook.advanceWhen: Each team has at least two evidence-backed implications.

steps.label: BOUNDARY
steps.title: What is inside the system—and what is not?
steps.lead: Scope becomes technical when you define the boundary.
choices: INSIDE — the system must do this
UNCERTAIN — we need evidence before deciding
steps.studentTask: Build three columns for your project: Inside / Outside / Uncertain. Place your major functions, decisions, and integrations into one of the three.
steps.visualCaption: If everything is inside the system, the scope is probably not real.

runbook.openWith: Before we draw boxes and arrows, decide what your system is accountable for.
runbook.whyMatters: Forces scope discipline before component design.
runbook.ask: What function are you tempted to include that does not actually need to be in Semester 1?
runbook.listenFor: Clear ownership, client systems, human decisions, external APIs, data stores, non-goals.
runbook.ifTheySay: It depends → move it to Uncertain and define what evidence resolves it.
runbook.ifQuiet: Ask what the prototype can safely exclude and still test the core value.
runbook.pushFurther: What would break if this item moved outside the boundary?
runbook.sayDuringReveal: Uncertain is a legitimate architecture state when the missing evidence is named.
runbook.transition: With the boundary set, map the flow through the system.
runbook.studentDoes: Defines in-scope, out-of-scope, and unresolved system responsibilities.
runbook.askNext: What enters the system, what happens to it, and what leaves?
runbook.watchFor: Feature wish lists disguised as scope.
runbook.ifStuck: Start with the user action and work inward.
runbook.advanceWhen: Each team has a defensible boundary and at least one named non-goal.

steps.label: MAP
steps.title: Trace the system from user need to human decision.
steps.lead: Users → Inputs/Data → AI/Logic → Systems → Output → Human Decision
steps.studentTask: Create a first-pass architecture map using the six-part flow. Name actual systems and data where known; label unknowns instead of inventing them.
steps.roomInstruction: USER / NEED → INPUTS & DATA → AI / LOGIC → SYSTEMS → OUTPUT → HUMAN DECISION
steps.visualAccent: Map the flow. Label the unknowns.
steps.visualCaption: Architecture is a hypothesis about how value, data, logic, and decisions move through a system.

runbook.openWith: Your diagram does not need to be pretty. It needs to make the proposed flow challengeable.
runbook.whyMatters: Creates a concrete artifact for expert review and next-phase work.
runbook.ask: Where does information enter? Where is AI actually adding value? Where does a person still decide?
runbook.listenFor: Named inputs, transformations, model/agent roles, APIs, storage, client systems, outputs, human review.
runbook.ifTheySay: AI does the analysis → ask which model or logic, using what inputs, producing what decision-support artifact.
runbook.ifQuiet: Walk the flow left to right and force one label per stage.
runbook.pushFurther: Which arrow represents the highest-risk assumption?
runbook.sayDuringReveal: Do not hide uncertainty with generic labels like platform, AI, or database. Name what you know and mark what you do not.
runbook.landHere: A useful architecture map exposes decisions and unknowns.
runbook.transition: Now Parker gets to attack the map.
runbook.askNext: Which part would an expert challenge first?
runbook.watchFor: Boxes without data flow or human decision points.
runbook.ifStuck: Use verbs on arrows: retrieve, classify, compare, generate, verify, display.
runbook.advanceWhen: Each team can narrate the flow in under 60 seconds.

steps.label: CHALLENGE
steps.title: Expert challenge: where does this architecture fail?
steps.lead: Commit first. Then invite the attack.
steps.studentTask: Present your architecture in 60 seconds. Parker challenges the weakest assumption, integration, component, or handoff. Capture the challenge and your response.
steps.visualAccent: Do not defend the diagram. Improve the decision.
steps.visualCaption: The goal of expert feedback is not approval. It is to expose fragility before build.

runbook.openWith: Parker, I want you to attack the architecture—not solve it for them.
runbook.whyMatters: Keeps students as owners while using expert judgment as a pressure test.
runbook.ask: What assumption here would make you nervous if this were going into production?
runbook.listenFor: Integration feasibility, data access, latency, model behavior, security, observability, maintainability, testing, human oversight.
runbook.ifTheySay: We can figure that out later → ask whether later means prototype risk or production detail.
runbook.ifQuiet: Ask Parker to choose one arrow and ask what has to be true for it to work.
runbook.pushFurther: What is the smallest experiment that could reduce this uncertainty this week?
runbook.sayDuringReveal: Expert input becomes valuable only when it changes a decision, test, or risk.
runbook.landHere: Feedback should produce a revision or a testable question.
runbook.transition: Now separate architecture facts from architecture assumptions.
runbook.studentDoes: Receives expert critique and captures a specific architecture revision or test.
runbook.askNext: What are we currently treating as true without enough evidence?
runbook.watchFor: Students becoming passive while Parker designs the system.
runbook.ifStuck: Require the team to answer before Parker offers a recommendation.
runbook.advanceWhen: Each team has one expert challenge and one resulting action.

steps.label: ASSUMPTIONS
steps.title: Which architecture choices are still bets?
steps.lead: If it has not been verified, label it.
choices: TESTABLE — can reduce uncertainty this week
steps.studentTask: Identify your top three architecture assumptions. Classify each as Known, Assumed, Blocked, or Testable. Pick the one with the highest consequence if wrong.
steps.visualCaption: Architecture quality improves when uncertainty is explicit.

runbook.openWith: Every architecture has assumptions. The danger is pretending assumptions are facts.
runbook.whyMatters: Turns uncertainty into managed project work.
runbook.ask: Which assumption would force the biggest redesign if it is wrong?
runbook.listenFor: API access, data quality, model accuracy, response time, user behavior, permissions, integration constraints.
runbook.ifTheySay: We think it should work → mark it Assumed until evidence says otherwise.
runbook.ifQuiet: Ask what they have not personally tested, observed, or confirmed.
runbook.pushFurther: Can you design a one-hour or one-day test instead of debating it?
runbook.sayDuringReveal: A testable assumption is not a weakness. An invisible assumption is.
runbook.landHere: The next build work should reduce uncertainty, not merely add features.
runbook.transition: Now look at the risks that could make a technically working system unacceptable.
runbook.studentDoes: Classifies assumptions and chooses the highest-consequence uncertainty.
runbook.askNext: What could work technically and still fail the client or user?
runbook.watchFor: Calling client statements verified technical facts.
runbook.ifStuck: Use the phrase: We believe ___ because ___; we still need to verify ___.
runbook.advanceWhen: Each team has one high-priority assumption and a verification move.

steps.label: RISK
steps.title: What could work technically and still fail?
steps.lead: Check privacy, access, accuracy, integration, feasibility, and experience.
steps.studentTask: Select the two risk categories most likely to threaten your current architecture. Name the specific risk and one safeguard, test, or design response.
steps.roomInstruction: RISK = LIKELIHOOD × CONSEQUENCE · NAME THE RESPONSE
steps.visualAccent: A prototype can be impressive and still be unsafe, unusable, or unintegratable.
steps.visualCaption: Risk review is part of architecture—not a cleanup step after the build.

runbook.openWith: Now assume the diagram works. What could still make it a bad system?
runbook.whyMatters: Keeps client, user, and operational risk inside technical decision-making.
runbook.ask: Which two risks deserve architecture-level treatment now?
runbook.listenFor: PII, restricted data, hallucination, inaccurate retrieval, inaccessible systems, integration bottlenecks, poor UX, missing escalation.
runbook.ifTheySay: We will add a disclaimer → ask whether the architecture itself should prevent or detect the failure.
runbook.ifQuiet: Fidelity: where must expert financial judgment stay in the loop? CMC: what happens when recognition or collection lookup is wrong in front of a visitor?
runbook.pushFurther: What signal would tell you this risk is actually occurring?
runbook.sayDuringReveal: A real safeguard changes the system, workflow, test, or ownership—not just the wording.
runbook.transition: You now have enough to make a gate decision.
runbook.studentDoes: Identifies two architecture risks and concrete responses.
runbook.askNext: Do we have enough evidence to move into prototyping?
runbook.watchFor: Generic risks without a design response.
runbook.ifStuck: Ask what failure a real user would notice first.
runbook.advanceWhen: Each team has two named risks and one response for each.

steps.label: GATE
steps.title: Make the call: are we ready to move forward?
steps.lead: Progression is based on evidence, not the calendar.
choices: GO WITH CONDITIONS — proceed while named gaps are resolved
NOT READY — key uncertainty must be reduced first
steps.studentTask: Choose a gate status for your team. Defend it with three pieces of evidence and name any condition that must be resolved.
steps.roomInstruction: GO · GO WITH CONDITIONS · NOT READY
steps.visualAccent: The calendar does not get a vote.
steps.visualCaption: A defensible decision names the evidence, remaining uncertainty, and consequence of proceeding.

runbook.openWith: Week 5 does not automatically mean you are ready to build. The question is whether the evidence supports moving forward.
runbook.whyMatters: Applies the Studio milestone-gate model and prevents premature implementation.
runbook.ask: What evidence justifies your gate decision?
runbook.listenFor: Discovery evidence, architecture clarity, testable unknowns, manageable risks, client alignment.
runbook.ifTheySay: GO because we need to start building → ask for evidence, not schedule pressure.
runbook.pushFurther: What would change your decision from GO WITH CONDITIONS to NOT READY?
runbook.sayDuringReveal: GO WITH CONDITIONS is often the most mature answer when the conditions are explicit and owned.
runbook.landHere: A gate decision is useful only if it changes what happens next.
runbook.transition: Finish by assigning ownership to the uncertainties that matter.
runbook.studentDoes: Makes and defends a milestone gate decision.
runbook.askNext: Who owns the next evidence-producing move?
runbook.ifStuck: Use: We are ___ because evidence shows ___. Before ___, we must resolve ___.
runbook.advanceWhen: Each team has a gate status and named conditions.

steps.label: OWNERSHIP
steps.title: Leave with one owned architecture move.
steps.lead: No vague next steps. One owner. One artifact. One question reduced.
steps.studentTask: Each student completes: “I own ___ by next Studio. The evidence/artifact will be ___. It will reduce uncertainty about ___.”
steps.visualCaption: The next move should produce evidence—not just activity.

runbook.openWith: Do not leave with 'work on architecture.' Leave with an evidence-producing commitment.
runbook.whyMatters: Converts class decisions into accountable project movement.
runbook.ask: What will exist next week because you owned it?
runbook.listenFor: Architecture diagram revision, API test, data-access confirmation, retrieval test, model evaluation, integration spike, risk test, client question.
runbook.ifTheySay: I will research ___ → ask what artifact or decision the research will produce.
runbook.ifQuiet: Use the stem exactly as shown.
runbook.pushFurther: Can someone else verify completion from the artifact?
runbook.sayDuringReveal: Hours are not the deliverable. The artifact and the reduced uncertainty are.
runbook.landHere: Evidence over assumptions. Progress over activity. Ownership over waiting.
runbook.watchFor: Shared ownership with no named person.
runbook.ifStuck: Force one noun: diagram, test, decision log, API result, risk matrix, client answer.
runbook.advanceWhen: Every student has one owner-level next move.
